newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No quick end seen to Brussels bourse rally.
newsitem.headline: No quick end seen to Brussels bourse rally.

text.p: The Brussels bourse ended Tuesday on a new record high on the shoulders of Wall Street's gains and a strong dollar with no near end seen to its aggressive rise.
"Things keep turning out well for the index, there's just no bad news for the bourse," said a dealer.
Dealers said the index would push past 1,900 level within days, with one dealers expecting it on Wednesday.
The Bel-20 share index ended 0.47 percent or 8.81 points higher to close at 1,896.55 after Monday's 1,887.74 close.
Trade was heavy with 2.97 billion francs worth of Belgian shares changing hands.
One dealer said that the Bel-20 index could easily be pushed beyond 1,900 points by fund managers' traditional end-of-year buying.
"So far the index is doing great and if it continues we'll go well beyond 1,900, we could even make it to 2,000," he said.
Others were more cautious but still expected the index to climb to 1,900.
"Investors are showing increased interest in cyclical stocks, but financials are also performing well," one said.
Steel wire and cord maker Bekaert was the day's leading victim, falling 5.2 percent to 23,625 francs on an unusually high volume of 17,966 shares.
The slide followed reports that U.S. chemicals giant Dupont had produced a fibre substitute for steel cords in tyres, reducing the weight of a tyre by up to 30 percent.
"This is a reaction to the publicity of Dupont," Bekaert's vice-president Willy Snaet told Reuters.
"It will soon pick up again," he added.
Dealers said Bekaert's losses prevented the Bel-20 from reaching 1,900 points.
Elsewhere among cyclicals the trend was upwards with utility firm Electrabel up 1.87 percent to 7,610 francs, with Generale Bank recommending investors to buy the share.
"Electrabel's gross dividend yield -- 6.36 percent -- has become extremely attractive to bond yields," the bank said.
Non-ferrous metals producer Union Miniere gained 1.6 percent to 2,225 francs and chemicals firm Tessenderlo added 2.1 percent to 13,475 francs.
